info.title: Chat Server API
info.description:
HTTP API of the PHP chat server (`index.php`).

## How this API really works

The server exposes **one single endpoint**. Every call is dispatched by a
key named `request`:

* **GET** requests carry `request=<name>` plus all other arguments as
  query parameters.
* **POST** requests carry everything â€” including `request` â€” in a
  **JSON body**.

Because `.htaccess` rewrites every path that is not an existing file or
directory to `index.php`, the path itself is irrelevant to the server:

```apache
RewriteEngine On
RewriteBase /~chkohl/chat/
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
RewriteRule . index.php [L]
```

`RewriteBase` must match the URL path of the installation directory
(e.g. `/` when served from the web root); without it, user-directory
installations (`/~user/...`) answer every virtual path with 404.

The paths used in this document (`/login`, `/getmessages`, â€¦) are
therefore **virtual**: they exist only so that each command can be
documented, and tried out, on its own. What actually selects the command is
the `request` parameter, which is pre-filled on every operation below.
Calling `GET /?request=login&...` is exactly equivalent to
`GET /login?request=login&...`.

## Authentication

Authentication is token based. `register` and `login` return a `token`;
every other command (except `ping` and `clear`) expects it as the `token`
argument. Use the **Authorize** button to set it once for all operations.
A token is invalidated by `logout`.

Some commands accept an additional `key` argument, the **admin key**. It is
verified against a password hash compiled into the server and unlocks
extra data (real user ids, all chats regardless of membership) or
privileged commands.

## Response format

Every JSON response contains at least `status` (`ok` or `error`) and
`code`. Successful responses are HTTP 200 with `status: "ok"`. Errors are
returned with the application error code **as the HTTP status code**, which
is why non-standard statuses such as `451`â€“`469` appear below. Error
responses always carry a human readable `message`.

Two commands do not return JSON: `getphoto` returns `image/png` and
`getfile` returns the stored binary with a `Content-Disposition` header.

## Character restrictions

User ids must match the HSE login scheme: four letters, `it`, two digits
(e.g. `abcdit01`), case insensitive.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the directory containing index.php, e.g. https://example.org/chat

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: Posting and reading messages, photos and files

tags.name: Service
tags.description: Connectivity checks and the built-in manual

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: Commands that require the admin key. They are not advertised by the server's own error messages.

get.description: A GET without a `request` parameter (and a POST without a JSON body) returns `manual.html`, the short built-in reference of all commands.

get.summary: Check that the server is alive
get.description: The only command that needs neither token nor admin key.

Creates the account and immediately logs it in: the response contains a valid token. The returned `hash` is the user's public identifier â€” it is what other users need in order to invite this user to a chat.

parameters.name: userid
parameters.description: HSE login id â€” four letters, `it`, two digits.

451.description: Wrong user id â€” must be the HSE login userid (8 chars)

get.summary: Log in and obtain a token
get.description: Returns a new token; previously issued tokens stay valid until they are logged out. If the account has no password hash (for example after an admin `resetuser`), the password supplied here becomes the new password.

get.summary: Check whether a token is still valid
get.description: Always answers with HTTP 200 and `status: "ok"` â€” the actual result is in `message`, which is either `Token valid` or `Token NOT valid`. The server delays the answer by one second to slow down brute force attempts.
Removes the user file. Messages already written by the user and chat memberships are **not** removed â€” use the admin command `deleteuser` for that.

post.summary: Post a message to a chat
post.description:
The only POST command: all arguments, including `request` and `token`,
are sent in the JSON body.

A message may carry any combination of text, one photo, one file and a
position; all of them are optional. Photo and file are sent inline as
base64 and are stored separately â€” the message then only references them
via `photoid` / `fileid`, which are fetched with `getphoto` / `getfile`.

Text is sanitised server side: HTML tags and NUL bytes are stripped and
quotes are replaced by HTML entities.

text.description: Message text. Non-string values are treated as empty.

photo.description: PNG image as base64, with or without the `data:image/png;base64,` prefix.

file.description: Arbitrary file as base64, with or without a `data:<mime>;base64,` prefix. The type is detected from the leading bytes (PDF, ZIP/DOCX, DOC, PNG, JPEG, otherwise `application/octet-stream`).

chatid.description: Target chat. 0 is the main chat.

important.description: Marks the message as important. Accepts `true`/`false`, `"true"`/`"false"` and `1`/`0`.

get.description: Returns all messages of the chat whose id is **greater than** `fromid`. Poll with the highest `id` received so far to fetch only new messages.

parameters.name: fromid
parameters.description: Return only messages with a higher id. Defaults to 0 (all).

parameters.name: chatid
parameters.description: Chat to read from. 0 is the main chat.

get.description: Returns the raw PNG referenced by a message's `photoid`. The response is an image, not JSON â€” errors, however, are still returned as JSON.

parameters.name: photoid
parameters.description: Photo id taken from a message's `photoid` field.

get.description: Returns the file referenced by a message's `fileid`. The content type comes from the stored metadata (falling back to `application/octet-stream`), together with a `Content-Disposition: attachment` header.

parameters.name: fileid
parameters.description: File id taken from a message's `fileid` field.

get.description: Returns every registered user that has a hash and a nickname. Password hashes and token lists are never included.
Returns the main chat (id 0) plus every chat the user owns, is a member of, is invited to, or that is public. With a valid admin `key`, all chats are returned.
The caller becomes the owner of the new chat. The new chat id is returned; ids are handed out consecutively.

parameters.name: chatname
parameters.description: Name of the chat, at least 2 characters.

parameters.name: ispublic
parameters.description: A public chat can be joined by anyone without an invitation and is listed for every user.

parameters.name: directchat
parameters.description: A direct chat is a one-to-one chat: only a single user can ever be invited to it.

get.description: Only the owner of the chat â€” or a caller with a valid admin `key` â€” may delete it. The chat and all its messages are removed.

460.description: Not the chat owner, or the chat does not exist

get.description: Succeeds if the chat is public or the user has been invited; a pending invitation is consumed. Owners and members may call it again without effect.

458.description: Invalid chat id, or the chat is private and the user is not invited

get.description: Removes the user from the members and invited lists. The owner cannot leave â€” they delete the chat instead â€” and nobody can leave the main chat (id 0).

parameters.name: chatid
parameters.description: Chat to leave. Must not be 0.

461.description: May not leave â€” either the owner (use deletechat) or not a member

get.summary: Invite a user to a chat
get.description: Only the chat owner â€” or a caller with a valid admin `key` â€” may invite. The invited user is identified by their public `hash`, as returned by `getprofiles`. A direct chat accepts only one invitation in total.

parameters.name: invitedhash
parameters.description: Public hash of the user to invite.

458.description: Invalid chat id, not the chat owner, or a direct chat that already has an invitation

get.description: Invitations to the main chat (id 0) are never listed.

458.description: Invalid chat id, or no invitation for this chat

get.summary: Reset a user's password and tokens
get.description: Clears the password hash and all tokens of the given user. The next `login` for that account then sets a new password. Requires a valid admin `key` in addition to the caller's own token.

get.summary: Delete a user with all their data
get.description: Deletes the user account and, unlike `deregister`, also removes all their messages and their memberships in every chat. Requires a valid admin `key`.

get.summary: Delete all data on the server
get.description: Irreversibly removes all users, photos, messages and chats as well as the error log. Requires a valid admin `key`; no token is needed.

token.name: token
token.description: The token returned by `register` or `login`, sent as the query parameter `token`. For the POST command `postmessage` the token is part of the JSON body instead.

ChatId.name: chatid
ChatId.description: Id of the chat. 0 is the main chat.

AdminKey.name: key
AdminKey.description: Optional admin key. When valid, the response contains additional data that is otherwise hidden.

RequiredAdminKey.name: key
RequiredAdminKey.description: Admin key. The command fails with 459 if it is not valid.

UserHash.name: userhash
UserHash.description: Public hash of the user the command acts on.

StatusResponse.description: Envelope shared by every JSON response.

message.description: Human readable result or error description.

code.description: Application status code. 200 on success; on failure it mirrors the HTTP status code of the response.

token.description: Session token, 8 characters. Send it with every other command.

hash.description: The user's public identifier, 8 characters. Other users need it to invite this user to a chat.

Message.description: A single message. `id` is unique within its chat and increases monotonically â€” use the highest one seen as `fromid` when polling.

text.description: Sanitised message text. Absent if the message carries no text.

photoid.description: Id for `getphoto`, or null if the message has no photo.

fileid.description: Id for `getfile`, or null if the message has no file.

position.description: Geo position as sent by the client, e.g. `{lat: 48.739, lon: 9.307}`. Absent if none was sent.

usernick.description: Nickname of the author, resolved at read time.

username.description: Login id of the author. Only present with a valid admin key.

Profile.description: A user profile as returned by `getprofiles` â€” every stored user attribute except the password hash and the token list.

hash.description: Public identifier, used to invite this user.

ChatParticipant.description: Short profile of a chat owner, member or invitee.

Chat.description: A chat as seen by the calling user. The main chat (id 0) is a special case: it is always public and joined, has no `invited` list, and its `owner` and `participants` are returned as empty arrays.

visibility.description: A public chat may be joined by anyone; a private chat requires an invitation.

role.description: Role of the calling user in this chat.

joined.description: True if the calling user is owner or member.

directchat.description: One-to-one chat â€” only a single user can be invited.

owner.description: Profile of the chat owner. An empty array for the main chat and for chats whose owner no longer exists.

participants.description: Owner and members of the chat. Empty for the main chat.

invited.description: Users invited but not yet joined. The key is absent for the main chat.

Invite.description: A pending invitation as returned by `getinvites`.

MissingParameter.description: A required parameter is missing (403) or empty (404). The server also answers 400 when `request` itself is missing, 401 for an unknown request name, 402 for illegal characters and 405 for a non-numeric value where a number is required.

example.message: Request 'login' must contain a 'password' parameter ('The users password')

InvalidToken.description: Invalid token â€” log in again.

InvalidChatId.description: Invalid chat id â€” the chat does not exist.

NoAdmin.description: No admin â€” the supplied key is not valid.
